summary:
Isole is a region of Italy and stands under the national framework of Italy; no region-specific legal regime governing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified in the sources, and the national assessment applies.

Regional violence: on 26 April 2025, three young men were beaten at a fast-food restaurant in Catania because they were gay. The Procura etnea reconstructed a sequence of insults and threats preceding the physical assault, and video of the attack circulated publicly. A Catania-based outlet's 5 June 2026 follow-up, 'Omofobia in Sicilia, continuano le violenze', catalogued continuing assaults and suicide cases across Sicilian towns, indicating the 2025 pattern of attacks has not stopped.

Prison conditions affecting trans detainees, documented in a 2013 la Repubblica investigation, describe trans women held in men's sections because their identity cards still list them as male; female hormones cannot be prescribed to detainees whose ID says male, decisions pass between prison directors and doctors with no national guideline, and some facilities allow hormone treatment only if the detainee pays for it. Placement follows legal/registered sex rather than gender identity.

In January 2010 Italy announced plans to open one of the world's first prisons dedicated to transgender inmates at Pozzale, near Florence in Tuscany, converting an almost empty medium-security prison to house trans inmates mainly convicted of drug-related offences and prostitution; Italian gay-rights groups welcomed the move. Per 2013 reporting the plan was never realized, so no dedicated trans facility exists and trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.
tangentialFactors:
The 2026 Sicilian follow-up reporting places the Catania assault within a wider, continuing pattern of homophobic violence across Sicilian towns rather than an isolated event.

The Pozzale proposal, had it proceeded, would have been among the world's first dedicated transgender prison facilities; its non-implementation leaves Italy without such a facility.
localsOnly:
Trans women in Italian prisons, including those in this region, are held in men's sections where identity documents list them as male; hormone prescription is governed by no national guideline and some facilities require the detainee to pay for treatment.

The announced Pozzale facility near Florence was never realized, so trans prisoners continue to be placed in ordinary facilities.
outOfScopeNotes:
The la Repubblica investigation is from 2013 and the Pozzale reporting from 2010 and 2013; whether Italian prison practice on hormone access and placement has since changed is unresolved in the sources provided.

The sources do not document any region-specific statute, administrative practice or court ruling of Isole on gender recognition, facilities access or discrimination; the national framework carried by the parent record governs.
